clue.text: Tapestry shows a little demon out of the Orient

indicators.note: out of here reads as outside of, the demon standing round the eastern letter

parts.note: a goblin is a small mischievous demon of folklore
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A woven hanging depicts a small imp from the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' looks like the link to the definition; 'out of' is read as outside, the demon standing around the eastern letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobelin is the name of a famous Paris factory's woven wall hangings, a classic kind of tapestry.

clue.text: Heavenly sign falls and rises after midnight in this school

indicators.note: after puts the sign following the letter from midnight

parts.note: the middle of the word night is the letter G
the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: rises in a down entry means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the same zodiac sign used a second time

explanation.surface: A star sign sinks and climbs after midnight at a certain school.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry RAM 'falls' reading down and 'rises' reading up as MAR; G, the centre of 'night', comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A selective British secondary school is a grammar school, so the word stands for that kind of school.

clue.text: Spin-off of manufacturer's sales talk, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by how they are said

parts.note: a maker's pitch would be 'buy product'

explanation.surface: A side benefit from a factory's marketing patter.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary result arising incidentally from making something else, a side effect.

clue.text: Old form of street lighting, of course

explanation.surface: Old torches lit the streets, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Links were torches of tow and pitch carried by link-boys to light the way; a golf links is a seaside course.
explanation.definitionFit: Torches once carried through dark streets had this name, and a seaside golf course is also called this.

clue.text: Youth made a bloomer

explanation.surface: A young man made a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake, but it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The handsome Greek youth who fell for his own reflection, and the daffodil genus named after him.

clue.text: Partnership accountant sounds derisive

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant
hoots are jeering, scornful noises

explanation.surface: A business partner who keeps the books makes mocking noises.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in league with someone, a secret alliance, is the idiom 'in cahoots'.

clue.text: One way to travel to Wagner's Ring for instance?

explanation.surface: Asking about a means of getting to a Wagner opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle is one means of travel, and Wagner's four linked Ring operas form a series of works.

clue.text: Reversal of normal position worker has to endure

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
to stand something is to endure it

explanation.surface: A labourer's position is unnatural and must be tolerated.
explanation.definitionFit: Balancing upside down on one's palms turns the body's usual upright stance on its head.

clue.text: Like Mary's follower one's about six

indicators.note: about means the word one goes round the numeral

parts.note: the word one, with 's as is
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Mary's little lamb, the one that followed her, is roughly six.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Mary had a little lamb' gives the follower, and the answer means sheep-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Her follower in the rhyme is a lamb, so the adjective for sheep fits.

clue.text: Ghost of the tax-man dropping in, say?

indicators.note: say signals that what follows is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a tax inspector who drops the letters IN leaves SPECTOR

explanation.surface: Asking whether the tax inspector calling round is a phantom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping in' looks like a visit, but it removes IN from INSPECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparition or phantom haunting the living.

clue.text: Tree in a southern enclosure

parts.note: a pen is a fenced enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A tree stands inside a fenced pen in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: The quaking poplar, with its trembling leaves, is a tree of this name.

clue.text: Abstruse ceremony incorporates second decapitation

indicators.note: incorporates means the ceremony word takes the other piece into its body

parts.note: a rite is a solemn ceremony

indicators.note: decapitation cuts the head, the opening letter, off the word second

parts.note: taken as written before its head is cut off

explanation.surface: An obscure ritual involves beheading someone a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitation' removes the head letter of 'second', and 'incorporates' sets what remains inside the ceremony word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe knowledge that is obscure and hard for an ordinary person to grasp.

clue.text: Unlawful spirits seen by night? Nonsense!

explanation.surface: Bootleg liquor glimpsed in the dark is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicitly distilled whisky, the pale light of the lunar disc at night, and foolish talk all share this one word.

clue.text: Proverbially white paper

explanation.surface: Something traditionally pale is a piece of stationery.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile 'white as a sheet' makes it proverbially pale, and a single leaf of stationery is also called this.

clue.text: But not describing the ring in which it is fought

definitions.text: But not describing the ring in which it is fought

parts.words: But not describing the ring in which it is fought
parts.note: a boxing bout is divided into timed sessions sharing a name with a circular shape, yet the boxing ring itself is square

explanation.surface: A remark that something is not a fair description of the arena where a bout takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: A session of a boxing match bears the name of a circular shape, though the ring is actually square.

clue.text: Telephone item paid up a short time before annual meeting

indicators.note: before puts the time ahead of the meeting
up in a down entry means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
hr is the short form of hour
AGM is annual general meeting

explanation.surface: Part of a phone was paid for shortly before the yearly company meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A vibrating disc in a phone mouthpiece or earpiece is the diaphragm.

clue.text: Publish, by sections that is, Israel's Redevelopment

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds these letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
the name with its S, all letters used

explanation.surface: Israeli rebuilding is reported in instalments.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Israel's' counts as a letter here: IE plus ISRAELS gives the nine letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a story in instalments, piece by piece in successive issues, is to bring it out this way.

clue.text: But its glimmer too feeble for a first film showing?

definitions.text: But its glimmer too feeble for a first film showing?

parts.words: But its glimmer too feeble for a first film showing?
parts.note: a director's first daily prints are called rushes, and a candle made from a reed dipped in fat gives a feeble light

explanation.surface: A joke that some lamp is too dim to project a film's early prints.
explanation.walkthrough: Rushes are the first prints of a day's filming; a rushlight is a cheap candle of rush pith dipped in tallow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap, dim taper made of a reed soaked in fat.

clue.text: Urge soldier to rise and enter in state

indicators.note: enter means the soldier goes into the phrase in state

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to rise in a down entry means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is pressed to get up and come in ceremonially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns GI to IG; 'enter' puts it into IN STATE: INST + IG + ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur on or provoke something into being is to incite it.

clue.text: Dramatic emotional outlet in musical about "Hair's" characters

indicators.note: about means the musical's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Cats is the Lloyd Webber stage musical

indicators.note: characters here means the letters of the word are set out afresh in a new order

parts.note: the title with its S, all letters used

explanation.surface: A musical about the show Hair offers the cast an emotional release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like the people in the show, but it rearranges the title Hair's; 'about' puts the musical Cats round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle's term for the purging of pity and fear through tragedy, hence any emotional release.

clue.text: This throws light on strange secrets

indicators.note: strange signals the letters are in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Something illuminates odd hidden matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges SECRETS. A cresset is an iron basket of burning fuel used as a beacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal fire basket on a pole served as a beacon or torch.

clue.text: Some in turn, made so dopey, given medicine

indicators.note: in turn says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A patient drugged into a stupor has been given treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To be treated with a measured quantity of a drug is to have been administered a dose.

clue.text: In Chinatown reds riot in resort of criminals

indicators.note: riot suggests the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: a den is a haunt of thieves

explanation.surface: Communists cause disorder in a crooks' hideout in Chinatown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinatown' looks like a district, but it is a town famous for china: Dresden porcelain. 'riot' rearranges REDS to DRES.
explanation.definitionFit: The German city gave its name to a famous porcelain, so it is a town of china.

clue.text: Harold's mistress had a neck like Annie Laurie's

definitions.text: Harold's mistress had a neck like Annie Laurie's

parts.words: Harold's mistress had a neck like Annie Laurie's
parts.note: King Harold II's mistress was nicknamed Swan-neck, and the Scottish song says Annie Laurie's neck is like the swan

explanation.surface: A historical gossip note comparing a royal lover's neck to the heroine of a Scots song.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold II, killed at Hastings in 1066, had a mistress called Swan-neck; the song 'Annie Laurie' praises 'her neck is like the swan'.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman known as Swan-neck was King Harold's partner before the Norman Conquest.

clue.text: Likeness of one Melchior perhaps

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Melchior was one of the Magi, the wise men, so an example of a magus or mage

explanation.surface: A portrait of one of the Three Wise Men.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture or representation resembling someone.

clue.text: One diamond in game played on board

explanation.surface: A single gem is a pastime played on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewel set alone in a ring has this name, as does a one-player peg game on a board.

clue.text: Upset many mouthpieces

annotationWithheld.why: Upset many mouthpieces: L (many) + LIPS (mouthpieces) read upwards gives the answer, but 'Upset' is then both the reversal indicator and the definition

clue.text: Two cardinal points in Kipling's ballad for instance

definitions.text: cardinal points in Kipling's ballad for instance

explanation.surface: A pair of compass points named in a famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's 'Ballad of East and West' opens 'East is East, and West is West, and never the twain shall meet'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a pair, and East and West in Kipling's line are 'the twain'.

clue.text: Like sailors rectifying a fire snag

indicators.note: rectifying means putting these letters right, setting them in a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors are seen putting right a problem with a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rectifying' rearranges the nine letters of A FIRE SNAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariners' life is spent travelling by sea, so the adjective describes the nautical life.

clue.text: What the court gives to one it protects

explanation.surface: Something a judge hands down goes to the person under the court's care.
explanation.walkthrough: A ward of court is a minor under the court's protection, so 'one it protects' is A WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's decision of compensation or damages is this, and a child under court protection is a ward.

clue.text: Current of use to fliers who are without power

definitions.text: Current of use to fliers who are without power

parts.words: Current of use to fliers who are without power
parts.note: glider pilots, having no engine, rely on rising columns of warm air

explanation.surface: A remark about air currents that help pilots with no engines.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising column of heated air lifts gliders, which have no engine.

clue.text: Can a bird find the abbey?

parts.note: a tin is a metal can
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A question about whether a bird can locate a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: TINTERN Abbey is a ruined Cistercian abbey in the Wye valley in Wales, the subject of a Wordsworth poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous ruined Welsh monastery by the River Wye bears this name.
